blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Consumer prices grew 7.8 percent from a year earlier in October, driven by faster increases in transport costs and pricier utilities. The latest inflation rate was higher than the 7.2 percent recorded in September, data from the Philippine Statistics Authority showed. READ: Poll: October inflation seen hitting over 3-yr high of 7.6% The reading also surpassed the 7.6 percent median estimate of 19 economists surveyed by the Inquirer last week. The figure fell within the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) forecast range of 7.1 percent to 8.1 percent for October. Still, it was above the 3-percent target of the […]...
